about: How far each renderer may sit from reSIDfp in tools/sid-engines/run_matrix.py --check. Renders are deterministic, so a measured value only moves when an engine or this app's use of it changes; the margins are there to let a harmless change through and stop a real one. Each override names the tune by file stem and says why it differs.

overrides.reason: Gate retriggers faster than the envelope completes: the notes' onsets differ by a few samples, which moves the chroma of the short notes. reSIDfp against itself from another power-on state scores 0.98, so this is a libSidplayEZ difference, in the attack of retriggered notes.

Three chips play as libSidplayEZ's centred mono mix at the power reSIDfp gives uncorrelated chips (see the architecture document); this probe's chips are correlated, so the level and band balance differ.
HVSC: three chips, as three-sid. reSIDfp's two sides correlate at 0.88 here, against 1.0 for the centred mix.

HVSC: the envelope measure depends on the oscillators' start phase in this tune. reSIDfp against itself scores 0.60 to 0.90 depending on the power-on delay alone; chroma 0.99 and band error 0.1 dB show the same notes and timbre.
HVSC: subsong 10 starts 50 ms earlier (libSidplayEZ discards the audio of the init routine), and its envelope measure moves with start phase as Commando's does; reSIDfp against itself scores 0.82.
SIDLite plays 8580 volume-register samples about 4.5 dB louder than reSIDfp.
HVSC: SIDLite is a cheaper approximation; its envelopes diverge most on fast arpeggios.
HVSC: an 8-bit digi, played about 4 dB louder.
HVSC: multispeed, played about 3 dB louder.
HVSC: an NTSC RSID whose chroma similarity sits at 0.91.
HVSC: a BASIC tune; SIDLite starts it about 30 ms later.
SIDLite's 6581 filter is a simpler approximation; 0.69 over 20 s, 0.59 over 30 s.
As digi-8580: SIDLite plays 8580 volume-register steps about 4.5 dB louder than reSIDfp.
